title: Energies in the destiny matrix: what they are in plain words

seo.title: Energies in the destiny matrix: what they are and how to read them
seo.description: In the destiny matrix an energy is the arcanum-number working at a point of the chart: the centre, the year, the day. Here is the term in plain words.
queries: what are energies in the destiny matrix
destiny matrix energy of the year
types of energies in the destiny matrix

short: An energy in the destiny matrix is the everyday name for an arcanum-number (from 1 to 22) that stands at a particular point of the chart and works there. When people say “the energy of the centre”, “the energy of the year” or “my energy by date of birth”, they do not mean a separate mystical substance, but the same arcanum, only called by a simpler name and tied to the place where it shows up. So “energy” answers not the question “what number is this”, but the question “how does this number work right here”. The meanings of the numbers themselves are set out on the arcana pages; this overview page explains the term and shows how to read your energies without mixing them up with programs and chakras.

sections.h2: What people call an energy in the destiny matrix
paragraphs: The destiny matrix is built from the numbers 1 to 22 — these are the arcana. Each one lands in its own point: the centre, the corners, the family lines, the arcanum of the day, of the month and of the year. The word “energy” came into the method as a casual stand-in for the word “arcanum”: it is easier to say “my energy of the centre is such and such” than “the arcanum in the central position”. So the phrases “energy of the centre”, “energy of the year” and “energy by date of birth” are not different things, but one and the same arcanum, named after the point where it stands.

From this comes a simple rule of reading: an energy always has two addresses — a number and a place. The number says which arcanum it is: its character, its strong and weak sides. The place sets the question: centre E is about the basic inner state, point C from the digits of the birth year is about the material task, the day arcanum A is about the personality portrait. The same arcanum reads differently in different points, because what changes is not the number but the role of the position.

sections.h2: How an energy differs from an arcanum and from a program
paragraphs: An arcanum is the number itself and its meaning: what it carries in any position. The meaning of an arcanum does not depend on whose chart is being looked at, and it is set out on the page of that arcanum. An “energy” is the same arcanum, but taken at work, at a particular point of one chart. The difference is like the one between the dictionary meaning of a word and what that word means in a particular sentence: the dictionary stays the same, while the sense inside the phrase depends on the place.

A program is the third term, and it is the one most often confused with an energy. In the product it is the reading of a repeating scenario through three positions that have already been calculated: the karmic task D, the centre E and the spiritual purpose. The karmic tail M–N–D is another named route with a strict order. So not every energy and not any random three numbers become a “program”: first you need the specific context of a position.

sections.h2: The energy of the year: the fixed one and the personal one
paragraphs: People ask separately about the “energy of the year”, and two different things hide under that one name. The first is point C, calculated from the digits of the birth year: this is the fixed material task of the chart. The second is the arcanum of the personal calendar year, which is recalculated every year and sets the angle from which the period is read.

The personal year is counted from the date of birth and the current year, so the “energy of the year” for the same person will be different in 2025 and in 2026. That is a big topic of its own — which arcanum comes for the year and how to fit in with it is covered in the “for the year” category; here the only thing that matters is not to confuse the fixed arcanum of the birth year with the shifting energy of the personal year.

sections.h2: How to read your own energies
paragraphs: Reading any energy takes two steps. First you find the number: the arcanum of a point is worked out from the date of birth by the rules of calculation, and it is easier to get your chart in the calculator than to add everything up by hand. Then you look at the meaning of that arcanum on its page — the character, the strong and the weak sides. This is the answer to the question “which energy”.

The second step is to lay that meaning over the point. The same arcanum in the centre reads as the core of the character, in the position of relationships as a scenario inside a couple, in the day arcanum as a first impression. You take the meaning of the number ready-made, but you do the translation into the area of the point yourself: you ask not “what does this arcanum mean in general”, but “how does this trait show up right here”. The easiest place to start is the central energy — it is the support of the whole chart, and its own reading sits on the page of the centre.

The main myth is that energies split into “good” and “bad” ones. There are no bad arcana in the method: every number has a strong side and a weak one, and the “heaviness” of an energy is its unworked side, not a sentence. Frightening labels such as a “bad” or a “dark” energy describe nothing except the fact that the arcanum is still turned towards the person with its weak edge.

Another common mistake is to take “energy” literally, as a substance that can be “cleaned up” or “pumped up” with a rite. In the destiny matrix an energy is not a field and not a charge, but a metaphor for an arcanum at a point; “working with an energy” means noticing a trait and changing behaviour, not performing a ritual. And the third frequent mix-up is to blend energies with chakras: chakras are a separate map of seven levels with numbers of their own, not the same thing as the arcanum of a point.

faq.q: What is an energy in the destiny matrix in plain words?
faq.a: It is the casual name for an arcanum — a number from 1 to 22 that stands at some point of the chart and works there. The “energy of the centre” is simply the arcanum that landed in the centre; the “energy of the year” is the arcanum in the position of the year. There is no separate mystical substance behind the word.

faq.q: How does an energy differ from an arcanum?
faq.a: The arcanum is the bare number and its meaning, which stays the same in any chart. An energy is that same arcanum taken at work, at one particular point of one particular chart. You take the meaning from the page of the arcanum, and you call it an “energy” when you look at how it shows up in a given area.

faq.q: What is the energy of the year and why does it change?
faq.a: By the “energy of the year” people mean either the fixed point C from the digits of the birth year — the material task of the chart — or the arcanum of the personal calendar year, which is recalculated every year. The personal year is covered in detail in the “for the year” category.

faq.q: Are there bad or dark energies?
faq.a: No. Every arcanum has a strong side and a weak one; a “bad” energy is simply an arcanum that works with its weak edge for now, not a curse and not a sentence. Working on it changes not the number, but which side of it is turned towards you.

faq.q: Are energies and chakras the same thing?
faq.a: No, they are not. Chakras are a separate map of seven levels with numbers and a meaning of their own. The energy of a point is an arcanum in a position of the matrix. The two get confused often, because both words are about “energy”, but they are calculated and read in different ways.

faq.q: How do I find out my own energies?
faq.a: Calculate the chart from the date of birth, find the arcanum of the point you need and look at its meaning on the page of that arcanum, then read it for the area of that point. The fastest way is to get all the numbers at once in the calculator instead of counting by hand.
